manifest.description: Mutating rewrite that normalizes a method to use the correct callback-owned DSLContext — replacing provider lookups inside a transaction callback with config.dsl(), passing the transaction context into helper methods, and removing accidental mixed-context calls. Preserves nesting semantics unless the operator explicitly asks to flatten nested transactions.
when_to_use: java-jooq-dsl-context-audit identified mixed-context callbacks or provider lookups inside a transaction callback and the operator approves normalization
hardening a write path so the callback context is threaded through helper methods consistently
removing accidental Provider<DSLContext>.get() calls inside a transactionResult callback
anti_patterns: do not flatten nested transactions without explicit operator request — nesting semantics are operator-owned
do not change DSLContext qualifier across the rewrite — qualifier is fixed by the existing callback owner
do not infer read/write safety from method names or table names — policy is operator-supplied via the prior audit
do not apply when status=blocked or when apply is not explicitly true
do not invent helper method signatures from the user prompt — re-derive from the plan response

source.description: Java file containing the methods to normalize, relative to project_dir.

impl_name.description: Optional containing class name when source has multiple classes.

flatten_nested_transactions.description: Operator-supplied flag; only true when the operator explicitly approves flattening nested callbacks. MUST NOT be defaulted by the atom.

audit_plan_path.description: Optional path to the approved java_jooq_dsl_context_audit plan whose findings are being acted on.

validation_cmd.description: Validation command after apply. Defaults to ["mvn", "compile"].

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-jooq-transaction-boundary-normalize. Charter: rewrite selected methods to use the callback-owned DSLContext consistently; never flatten nested transactions unless explicitly authorized.

Protocol:

1. Ground the target structurally:
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{source}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")
   bbox_code_symbols(project_dir="{{project_dir}}", query="{{impl_name}}", languages=["java"], item_kinds=["class_declaration", "method_declaration"])
   Confirm every method in {{item_names}} resolves and contains a transaction callback.

2. Plan the normalization — PREVIEW only:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="java_jooq_transaction_boundary_normalize",
                      deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source="{{source}}",
                      impl_name="{{impl_name}}",
                      item_names={{item_names}},
                      toml_entries={"flatten_nested_transactions": {{flatten_nested_transactions}},
                                    "audit_plan_path": "{{audit_plan_path}}"})

   The planner refuses to flatten nested transactions when flatten_nested_transactions is not true. It preserves DSLContext qualifier and rewrites provider lookups, helper signatures, and mixed-context calls only where the callback owner is unambiguous.

3. Decide:
   - If status=blocked, emit bbox_note(kind="blocked") with block_reason and return.
   - If apply is not true, return status="planned".

4. Apply (only when inputs.apply == true):
   bbox_refactor_run(dispatch_origin="agent", confirm=true, steps=[
     <java_jooq_transaction_boundary_normalize step from the plan>,
     {"op":"command","command":"<validation_cmd[0]>","args":<validation_cmd[1..]>,"required":true}
   ])
   Default validation_cmd is ["mvn", "compile"].

5. Emit done note:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line: methods normalized, provider lookups replaced, helper signatures updated, nested flatten applied?, validation result>).

Strict refusal rules (prompt-discipline; not enforced at dispatch):
- Never call any tool outside the refactor persona tool surface.
- Never default flatten_nested_transactions — operator-authority is explicit.
- Never change DSLContext qualifier across the rewrite.
- Never infer read/write safety from method names or table names.
- Never default apply=true on the operator's behalf.

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{source}} {{impl_name}} {{item_names}} {{flatten_nested_transactions}} {{audit_plan_path}} {{apply}} {{validation_cmd}}
